record.original_question: For every positive integer n, the nth Mersenne number is M_n = 2^n - 1. Is every Mersenne number square-free?

evidence.quote: For every positive integer n, the nth Mersenne number is defined by M_n=2^n-1.
Hence, there remain several open problems about Mersenne primes: Is it that every Mersenne number happens to be square free?

artifact.self_contained_problem: For every positive integer $n$, define the $n$-th Mersenne number by $M_n = 2^n - 1$. A positive integer is said to be square-free if it is not divisible by the square of any prime. Determine whether $M_n$ is square-free for every positive integer $n$. Equivalently, decide whether there exists a prime $p$ and an integer $n \geq 1$ such that $p^2 \mid 2^n - 1$; in particular, decide whether $M_p$ is square-free for every prime $p$.
artifact.status_search_result: For general n, the answer is known to be negative: a prime p is called a Wieferich prime if p^2 divides 2^{p-1} - 1, and the known Wieferich primes 1093 and 3511 give 1093^2 | M_{1092} and 3511^2 | M_{3510}, so not every Mersenne number is square-free. However, the refined question — whether M_p is square-free for every prime p (in particular for Mersenne primes) — remains an open problem; no prime p is known for which M_p has a square factor, and it is conjectured that no Wieferich prime is itself a Mersenne exponent.

status_evidence.title: Wieferich prime - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: A Wieferich prime is a prime p such that p^2 divides 2^{p-1}-1; the known Wieferich primes are 1093 and 3511.
status_evidence.claim: Wieferich primes give explicit n with p^2 | M_n, so not every Mersenne number is square-free.

status_evidence.title: Mersenne prime - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: It is not known whether M_p is square-free for every prime p; this is related to the Wieferich-prime question among Mersenne exponents.
status_evidence.claim: Whether M_p is square-free for every prime p is an open problem.
